FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS
EASTERN DIVISION

RHYS MBEKI,

Case No. __________________

PLAINTIFF'S ORIGINAL COMPLAINT

TO THE HONORABLE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT JUDGE:

MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF ILLINOIS, LLC ("Meridian" or the "Company"), acting by and through its
undersigned counsel, files this Complaint against Defendants, and for causes of action would
respectfully show as follows:

NATURE OF THE ACTION

1. This is an action for breach of contract, trade secret misappropriation, and tortious
interference with contractual relations. The lawsuit arises out of two high-level former executives
of Meridian breaching their contractual obligations to the Company. The defendants also
misappropriated Meridian's confidential and trade secret information in violation of their legal
duties to the Company.

PARTIES

2. Plaintiff Meridian Mechanical of Illinois, LLC ("Meridian" or the "Company"), is an
Illinois limited liability company with a principal place of business located in Elk Grove Village,
Illinois. Meridian operates branch offices in Illinois, Texas, California, Washington, and other
locations nationwide.

3. Paige Hargrove ("Hargrove") is a former employee of Meridian. Upon
information and belief, Hargrove is a citizen of Texas, residing at 23800 Lloyd Lane, Hockley, Texas
77447.

4. Rhys Mbeki ("Mbeki") is a former employee of Meridian. Upon
information and belief, Mbeki is a citizen of Texas, residing at 1903 Sarah Cove, Taylor, Texas
76574.

5. Defendant Larkspur Capital, Inc. of Texas, LLC ("Larkspur Capital, Inc.") is a Texas
limited liability company, whose registered agent, Mr. Hargrove, is located at 23800 Lloyd
Lane, Hockley, Texas 77447. Upon information and belief, Hargrove is the sole owner of Alliance
Services.

JURISDICTION AND VENUE

6. This is a suit for a trade secret misappropriation under the Defend Trade Secrets
Act (the "DTSA"), 18 U.S.C. § 1836 et seq., the Illinois Freedom to Work Act (820 ILCS 90), the
Illinois Trade Secrets Act, and other related Illinois common law and statutory claims. This Court
has jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1338(a).

7. The Court has supplemental jurisdiction over Meridian's state law claims under
28 U.S.C. § 1367(a) because these claims are directly related to the claims in this action within
this Court's original jurisdiction and intertwined with the same case or controversy. Meridian's
common law claims are substantially related to Meridian's claims over which this Court has the
original jurisdiction.

8. This Court has personal jurisdiction over Hargrove and Mbeki as they both reside in
Texas, worked for Plaintiff in Texas, and breached their statutory, contractual, and common law
duties in Texas. The Court also has personal jurisdiction over Meridian's breach of contract
claims against Mbeki because in the agreement at issue she agreed to the jurisdiction of this Court.
This Court has personal jurisdiction over Larkspur Capital, Inc. as it is a domestic limited liability
company.

9. Venue is proper in this District pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) because a
substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to Meridian's claims occurred in this
District.

FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Meridian's Business

10. Meridian is in the business of providing a full spectrum of HVAC and plumbing
services to hundreds of brands and thousands of locations nationwide. Meridian's services include,
among other things, equipment services and repairs, diagnostics, maintenance and reporting, new
equipment sales and installation, and related services.

11. Meridian has developed certain proprietary, confidential and trade secret
information related to its business and the needs of its customers. This information is essential to
Meridian's continuing success.

12. Meridian has expended a substantial amount of time, money, and effort in
developing its confidential and trade secret information.

13. Meridian protects the secrecy of its confidential and trade secret information
by, among other things, requiring password and two-factor authentication protection of Meridian's
computers that have access to or contain such information; password protecting Meridian's
databases that contain such information; allowing access to it only to a restricted number of
Meridian employees with a specific need to know such information in order to perform their
job functions and who have an obligation to keep the information confidential; maintaining
policies with respect to the use and dissemination of such information; and restricting physical
access to Meridian's offices, IT systems, and facilities.

Hargrove's Duties at Meridian and His Access to Meridian's Confidential and Trade
Secret Information.

14. On May 1, 2022, Meridian entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement ("APA")
with Kessler Comfort Services ("Kessler Comfort Services") and its two shareholders.

15. Under the terms of the APA, Meridian purchased assets of Kessler Comfort Services.

16. Prior to the acquisition of Kessler Comfort Services by Meridian, Defendant Hargrove, son of one
of the owners of Kessler Comfort Services, had been employed by Kessler Comfort Services for more than 30 years.

17. Following the acquisition, Hargrove became an executive of Meridian, assuming a
role of Branch Operation Manager for the Company's Houston branch office.

18. In November of 2019, Meridian promoted Hargrove to the role of Regional
Director of Construction, the position he held at the time of his resignation from the Company in
May 2024.

19. Hargrove's position with Meridian was significant, and he was a critical employee
of Meridian.

20. As Regional Director of Construction, Hargrove was responsible for, among other
things, driving the profitability of the Company in the assigned region and achieving expected
business results, outstanding key performance indicators (KPIs), accurate forecasting and
workforce planning, and a high level of employee engagement and productivity.

21. As such, Hargrove's responsibilities included but were not limited to the following:
partnering with the Regional Vice President to drive regional initiatives and ensure the
Company's financial objectives were met; collaborating on strategic opportunities and assisting
the Construction Managers in achieving the Company's goals; identification and prioritization of
construction requirements with an objective of maintaining and driving construction operations
profitability; driving KPIs for Construction Managers to ensure operational efficiency; preparing
and participating in weekly, monthly, quarterly business reviews; identifying opportunities to
improve process and productivity; and managing and addressing customer issues.

22. As a result of his high-level position with the Company, Hargrove was intimately
familiar with Meridian's confidential and trade secret information including, but not limited
to, financial data regarding volumes of business and profitability of the Company's branch offices
in Texas, business strategies, financial and business projections, master files (providing average
costs per unit, current costs per unit, and highest costs per unit), existing bids on all projects, bid
sheets, actual job performance and budget plans, pricing and margins per customer, customer and
vendor contact information, and other confidential information pertaining to valuable, special, or
unique aspects of Meridian's business activities.

23. As part of his job duties, Hargrove also participated in confidential meetings, where
Meridian business strategies were discussed and created.

24. As one non-limiting example, Hargrove participated in the Company's leadership
summit that took place in Dallas on May 12-14, 2021, at which the Company's CEO shared
Meridian's sensitive information on strategy, operating trade secrets, and future growth and
vision. The invitation to the summit was limited to the Company's leaders.

25. The information to which Hargrove had access as part of his job at Meridian
constitutes commercially valuable information, is the subject of Meridian's efforts to maintain
secrecy or confidentiality and is not reasonably ascertainable through lawful means.

26. Hargrove would have been denied intimate access to Meridian's highly confidential,
competitively sensitive information but for his execution of the Hargrove Agreement as defined
below and position of trust and confidence with Meridian. Only those people in a need-to-
know position at Meridian are given access to such information.

27. Hargrove was a highly compensated employee at Meridian.

28. As a result of his high position with the Company, Hargrove owed the Company a
fiduciary duty including an undivided duty of loyalty to act in the Company's best interests, not
to compete with the Company during his employment with the Company, not to divert business
opportunities from the Company, and safeguarding the Company's confidential and competitive
business information and returning and not using such information at the end of his employment
with the Company.

29. Due to the critical position of Hargrove and to further protect the Company's
confidential business information, business relationship with the clients, and goodwill, at the time
of the purchase of assets and liabilities of Kessler Comfort Services by Meridian, Hargrove and Meridian,
entered into Confidential Information, Non-competition and Cooperation, Non-solicitation
Agreement ("Hargrove Agreement"). Meridian has not been able to locate a signed copy of the
Hargrove Agreement and suspects that Hargrove is in possession of the signed copy and that Hargrove
removed the signed copy of the Agreement at the time of his resignation from the Company. An
unsigned copy of the Hargrove Agreement is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

30. As part of consideration for entering into the Hargrove Agreement, and in addition to
employment with the Company, payment of compensation, and other employment-related
benefits, Meridian provided Hargrove with access to the Company's confidential information and
Hargrove obtained the knowledge of such confidential information.

31. Under the Agreement, Hargrove agreed to certain post-employment restriction,
including to limited noncompetition and non-solicitation restrictions:

During the Employee's employment with the Company and for a period of
twenty four (24) months following the termination of the Employee's
employment for any reason (the "Restricted Period"), the Employee (i) will not,
directly or indirectly, whether as an owner, director, officer, affiliate, creditor,
partner, shareholder, consultant, agent, principal, employee, employer, co-
venturer or otherwise in any individual or representative capacity, engage,
participate, assist, hold any interest in, or invest in any Competing Business (as
hereinafter defined) which is located or transacts business in Illinois, Michigan,
Wisconsin, Indiana, Hawaii, Florida or any other geographical area that the
Company may add to its portfolio during the term of the Employee's
employment; (ii) will refrain from directly or indirectly employing, attempting
to employ, recruiting or otherwise soliciting or inducing (or assisting others in
soliciting, inducing or influencing) any person to leave employment with the
Company and/or to terminate his or her remunerative relationship with the
Company as an agent or consultant of/to the Company (other than terminations
of employment of subordinate employees undertaken in the course of the
Employee's providing of services to the Company); and (iii) will refrain from
directly or indirectly soliciting (or assisting others in soliciting) any Company
customer (which includes prospective customers being actively solicited by the
Company at the time) which Employee provided service to, or which Employee
had personal contact with, during the last twenty-four (24) months of his
employment with the Company to terminate or otherwise modify adversely its
business relationship with the Company. The Employee understands that the
restrictions set forth in this Section 7(d) are intended to protect the Company
interest in its Confidential and Proprietary Information and established
employee, customer and supplier relationships and goodwill, and agrees that
such restrictions are reasonable and appropriate for this purpose. For purposes
of this Agreement, the term "Competing Business" shall mean any business or
company that principally engages in the Company Business and any other
business in which the Company engages in during the term of the Employee's
employment.

32. Meridian has performed its obligations under the Hargrove Agreement.

Mbeki's Duties at Meridian and Her Access to Meridian's Confidential and Trade
Secret Information.

33. On May 1, 2022, Meridian purchased assets of Kessler Comfort Services
("Kessler Comfort Services").

34. Prior to the acquisition of Kessler Comfort Services by Meridian, Mbeki had been employed by
Kessler Comfort Services.

35. Following the acquisition, Mbeki became an executive of Meridian assuming a
role of Office Manager of the Company's Austin branch office.

36. On July 12, 2024, Meridian promoted Mbeki to the position of Regional
Operations Manager.

37. Mbeki's positions with Meridian, both as Office Manager and Regional
Operations Manager, were significant, and she was a critical employee of Meridian.

38. As Regional Operations Manager, Mbeki was responsible for, among other things,
driving the profitability of the Company in the assigned region and achieving expected business
results, outstanding KPIs, accurate forecasting and workforce planning, and a high level of
employee engagement and productivity.

39. As such, Mbeki's responsibilities included but were not limited to the following:
partnering with the Regional Vice President to drive regional initiatives and ensure the
Company's financial objectives were met; collaborating on strategic opportunities and assisting
the Branch Managers in achieving the Company's goals; identification and prioritization of
construction requirements with an objective of maintaining and driving construction operations
profitability; driving KPIs for Branch Managers to ensure operational efficiency; preparing and
participating in weekly, monthly, quarterly business reviews; identifying opportunities to improve
process and productivity; managing and addressing customer issues.

40. As a result of her high-level position with the Company, Mbeki was intimately
familiar with Meridian's confidential and/or trade secret information including, but not limited
to, financial data regarding volumes of business and profitability of the Company's branch offices
in Texas, business strategies, financial or business projections, master files (providing average
costs per unit, current costs per unit, and highest costs per unit), pricing and margins per customer,
customer and vendor contact information, and other confidential information pertaining to
valuable, special, or unique aspects of Meridian's business activities.

41. As part of her job duties, Mbeki also participated in confidential meetings, where
Meridian business strategies were discussed and created.

42. Like Hargrove, Mbeki was also invited and participated in the Company's leadership
summit that took place in Dallas on May 12-14, 2021, where the Company's confidential
information was presented and discussed.

43. The information to which Mbeki had access as part of her job at Meridian
constitutes commercially valuable information, is the subject of Meridian's efforts to maintain
secrecy or confidentiality and is not reasonably ascertainable through lawful means.

44. Mbeki would have been denied intimate access to Meridian's highly confidential,
competitively sensitive information but for her execution of the Mbeki Agreement as defined
below and position of trust and confidence with Meridian. Only those people in a need-to-
know position at Meridian are given access to such information.

45. Mbeki was a highly compensated employee at Meridian.

46. As a result of her high position with the Company, Mbeki owed the Company a
fiduciary duty including an undivided duty of loyalty to act in the Company's best interests, not
to compete with the Company during her employment with the Company, not to divert business
opportunities from the Company, and safeguarding the Company's confidential and competitive
business information and returning and not using such information at the end of her employment
with the Company.

47. Due to the critical position of Mbeki and to further protect the Company's
confidential business information, business relationship with the clients, and goodwill, at the time
of the purchase of assets and liabilities of Kessler Comfort Services by Meridian, Mbeki and Meridian, as a
successor of Kessler Comfort Services, entered into Confidentiality and Stay Bonus Agreement ("Mbeki
Agreement"). Meridian has not been able to locate a signed copy of the Mbeki Agreement and
suspects that Mbeki is in possession of the signed copy and that Mbeki removed the signed copy
of the agreement at the time of her resignation from the Company. An unsigned copy of the Mbeki
Agreement is attached hereto as Exhibit B.

48. Meridian has performed its obligations under the Mbeki Agreement by paying
Mbeki the stay bonus, which she has accepted.

49. Under the Mbeki Agreement, Meridian has made and agreed to make available
to Mbeki certain Proprietary Information, as defined in the Mbeki Agreement, and provided to
Mbeki salary, bonuses, and other benefits of employment with the Company, and provided Mbeki
with the access to Proprietary Information specified in the Mbeki Agreement.

50. "Proprietary Information" in the Mbeki Agreement is defined as "information
regarding the Company, its subsidiaries and affiliates, including without limitation, financial
information, information regarding business plans, operations, strategies, suppliers, vendors,
pricing, and product plans, and, from time-to-time, its proprietary products and other proprietary
information, specifically including, but not limited to, knowledge of the potential or actual
acquisition of the Company." Exh. B, Sec. 1.

51. Mbeki agreed "to use the Proprietary Information solely for the purpose of providing
services to the Company, that the Proprietary Information will be kept confidential, and that
[Mbeki] will not disclose any of the Proprietary Information or in any manner whatsoever except
as contemplated [in the Mbeki Agreement]." Exh. B. Sec. 3.

52. Section 5 of the Mbeki Agreement provides that at the termination of Mbeki's
employment with the Company, Mbeki "shall immediately deliver all Proprietary Information
(including all copies, extracts or summaries thereof) to the Company."

53. In Section 6 of the Mbeki Agreement, Mbeki agreed to certain limited non-
solicitation restrictions providing in relevant part as follows:

during the period of Employee's employment by the Company and for a period of
one (1) year thereafter (hereinafter the "Protected Period"), except where such
actions are taken within the course and scope of Employee's employment with the
Company and in a manner the Employee reasonably believes to be in the best
interests of the Company, Employee will not, directly or indirectly, individually,
on Employee's own behalf or on behalf of another or through a corporate or other
business entity, (i) contact or otherwise communicate with any customer or supplier
on whom Employee called, with whom Employee communicated and/or as to
whom Employee provided any services or reviewed any information as a result of
Employee's employment with the Company within the preceding twelve (12)
months or, where Employee's employment with the Company has terminated, in
the twelve (12) months prior to the date his/her employment with the Company
terminated (hereinafter, a "Protected Customer/Supplier"); or (ii) influence or
attempt to influence any Protected Customer/Supplier to divert its business to any
individual, partnership, firm, corporation or other entity then in competition with
the business of the Company or any subsidiary or affiliate of the Company.

Exh. B, Sec. 6.

54. In Section 8 of the Mbeki Agreement, Mbeki agreed to certain limited non-
competition restrictions:

To further ensure the confidentiality of the Company's Proprietary Information, and
protect the Company's employee, customer and supplier related goodwill,
Employee shall not directly or indirectly (whether for compensation or otherwise),
alone or as a partner, associate, agent, principal, trustee, consultant, co-venturer,
creditor, owner (excepting not more than 1% stockholdings for investment
purposes in securities of publicly held and traded companies), representative, or in
any other capacity, engage in, take any action constituting or in furtherance of,
participate with or become interested in or associated with any person, firm,
partnership, corporation or other entity which is then in, or has expressed to
Employee the possibility of entering into, competition with the Company anywhere
in the State of Illinois, (i) during the period of Employee's employment by the
Company, or (ii) during the one year period thereafter, unless such person, firm,
partnership, corporation or other entity began operations, or was formed prior to
April 1, 2022.

Exh. B, Sec. 8.

55. Mbeki acknowledged that the foregoing covenants are appropriate and reasonable.
Exh. B, Sec. 10.

56. Mbeki also agreed that if she committed a breach, or threatened to commit a breach,
of any of the provisions of the Mbeki Agreement, Meridian shall have the right and remedy to
require Mbeki to account for and pay over to the Company all compensation, profits, monies,
accruals, increments or other benefits derived or received, directly or indirectly, by Mbeki as a
result of any transactions constituting a breach of any of the provisions of the Mbeki Agreement.
Exh. B, Sec. 11.

57. The Mbeki Agreement also provides that Meridian "shall be entitled to equitable
relief, including injunction and specific performance, as a remedy for any [breach of the Mbeki
Agreement], without having to post any bond or any other form of security, without having to
show any likelihood or irreparable harm, and without having to prove that money damages would
be an inadequate remedy." Exh. B, Sec. 12.

58. The Mbeki Agreement is governed and construed in accordance with the laws of the
State of Illinois. Exh. B, Sec. 15.

59. Mbeki also contractually agreed to the jurisdiction of this Court. Exh. B, Sec. 15.

Hargrove resigns from Meridian, then his replacement and Mbeki resign.

60. On March 26, 2024, Hargrove informed Meridian that he wanted to leave the
Company because, he stated, he did not enjoy working at a large company and because he was
tired of frequent work travel.

61. Desiring to keep Hargrove, Meridian took steps and addressed Hargrove's concerns by
reducing his travel commitments and allowing him to just manage the Company's Houston branch
office, something that Hargrove did before his promotion to the Regional Director role.

62. The Company did not reduce Hargrove's compensation and allowed to keep his title.
Hargrove decided to stay.

63. Yet, on May 18, 2024, Hargrove announced his resignation from the Company
providing a one-week notice via e-mail. At the time of his announced resignation, Hargrove spoke
with Isaac Radcliffe, Meridian's Vice President of Construction, and informed him that he
wanted to leave and that he was going to start his own business.

64. On May 20, 2024, Hargrove recommended to the Company that it should promote Joe
Kilgore ("Kilgore"), his long-time friend and a colleague, as his replacement. At that time,
Kilgore held the position of a General Construction Manager with the Company.

65. Hargrove's last day of employment with Meridian was May 25, 2024.

66. Less than a week later, on May 31, 2024, Meridian promoted Kilgore to the
Regional Director position.

67. Kilgore assumed the duties and responsibilities that previously were assigned to
Hargrove.

68. However, just two months later, in the end of July 2024, Kilgore also abruptly
announced his resignation.

69. Kilgore's last day of employment with Meridian was August 3, 2024.

70. Approximately one week later, Kilgore was spotted working a job with Hargrove on
behalf of Hargrove's new company.

71. In the meantime, on August 12, 2024, Mbeki sent an email to Fiona Falkner, Meridian's
Regional Vice President and her direct boss, announcing her decision to resign from the
Company. Mbeki proposed September 3, 2024, to be her last day of employment.

72. The announcement of Mbeki's resignation was made to the employees of Meridian
on August 17, 2024.

73. Between August 12, 2024, and September 3, 2024, Mbeki had numerous
conversations with the Company's employees during which she stated that she was leaving to
join her brother in his construction business, which was non-competitive to Meridian as it
involved remodeling offices in high rise buildings.

74. A few days after she announced her leaving, Mbeki also had a discussion with Todd
Ernest, Meridian's CEO, who asked her directly if she was going to work with Hargrove. Mbeki
responded, "What makes you think that?" and reiterated once again that she was going to work
for her brother's company.

75. Oddly, shortly before her departure from the Company, Mbeki made a request to the
Company for permission to print certain information relating to Meridian's existing bid pricing.
The Company denied the request.

76. Mbeki's last day of employment with Meridian was September 3, 2024.

Meridian Discovers that Hargrove and Mbeki Operate a Competing Business Serving
Meridian's Clients.

77. Following Mbeki's departure on September 3, 2024, Meridian started to receive
unsettling rumors that Hargrove, Kilgore, and Mbeki were now working together at Hargrove's new
company and targeting Meridian's customers.

78. Driftwood Enterprises, Inc. ("H-E-B") is a privately held supermarket chain
based in San Antonio, Texas, with more than 340 stores throughout Texas, as well as in northeast
Mexico.

79. DRIFTWOOD ENTERPRISES, INC. is one of the major customers of Meridian.

80. During their tenure at Meridian, both Hargrove and Mbeki serviced the H-E-B
account, including in the last twelve months of their respective employments at Meridian.

81. Specifically, Mbeki worked closely with H-E-B, dealing with business issues,
invoice disputes, and other related matters.

82. Hargrove, as Regional Director, participated in meetings with H-E-B discussing
construction contracts and business plans, and oversaw performance of construction jobs for H-
E-B.

83. On September 27, 2024, or more than three weeks after Mbeki's departure from
Meridian, Ms. Julie Healy of H-E-B sent an e-mail to Mr. Wes Seagroves at Trakref, a
company offering refrigerant management software, informing him that Defendant Alliance
Services was a new vendor working with H-E-B and acknowledging that Rhys Mbeki had
already contacted Trakref.

84. Ms. Healy copied Mbeki on the e-mail; however, she (perhaps accidentally) sent it
to Mbeki's Meridian work e-mail at rhys.mbeki@meridianmech.com, where it was discovered
by Meridian.

85. According to the records of the Texas Secretary of State, Larkspur Capital, Inc. was
registered on May 7, 2024, as an Illinois limited liability company, with Hargrove listed as its managing
member and registered agent and his home address at 2127 Market Street, Naperville, IL 60563
listed as the company's address.

86. According to the records of the Texas Secretary of State, on March 17, 2024, an
individual named Gregory Michael Hargrove residing at 2127 Market Street, Naperville, IL 60563
submitted an application for name reservation on behalf of Alliance Refrigeration of Texas, LLC
with the Texas Secretary of State.

87. Larkspur Capital, Inc.'s domain name at "asotx.com" was registered on May 16, 2024.

88. After discovering the evidence of Hargrove, Mbeki, and Larkspur Capital, Inc. unfairly
competing with Meridian, the Company hired legal counsel and a forensic computer expert
and launched an investigation relating to the circumstances of Hargrove's and Mbeki's departures,
including by forensically examining their work computers.

89. The forensic review of Mbeki's work computer revealed that on June 5, 2024, while
still employed by Meridian, Mbeki sent an e-mail to Hargrove advising Larkspur Capital, Inc. on how
to more effectively compete for customers ("I was playing around writing stuff last night and it's
not much but…. A few Kessler Comfort Services guys decided to keep the customer relationship strong and carry
on…we developed Larkspur Capital, Inc. of TX and want to carry that tradition on.")

90. Hargrove liked the idea responding two days later "I defiantly [sic] like it and we need
to incorporate it on the webpage."

91. Without disclosing to Meridian her association with Hargrove and Alliance
Services, and while continue to be employed and compensated by Meridian, Mbeki actively
assisted Larkspur Capital, Inc. to operate and compete with Meridian.

92. Mbeki's duplicitous activities are further manifested by her lying to the Company's
management and employees at the time of her announced resignation that she was going to join
her brother's business, when in fact she was going to join Larkspur Capital, Inc., the company for
which she acted as an agent as early as June 5, 2024, while still being an executive of Meridian
and receiving compensation from the Company.

Meridian Discovers Misappropriation of Its Confidential and Trade Secret Information
by Mbeki and Larkspur Capital, Inc.

93. The forensic investigation also revealed that on July 29, 2024, at 7:07 p.m., a Sony
Storage Media USB Device with a Serial Number 5A09112344160&0 ("Sony USB Device") and
the Associated User Account "rhys.mbeki" was connected to Mbeki's work computer and the document
"HEB MSA – CP.pdf" was accessed and opened.

94. "HEB MSA – CP.pdf" is a confidential document of Meridian. It is a copy of
the Master Services Agreement between Meridian and H-E-B ("H-E-B Master Services
Agreement"). Exhibit D to the DRIFTWOOD ENTERPRISES, INC. Master Services Agreement contains confidential business
information of Meridian such as rates of Meridian's technicians and helper technicians
(standard hours rates, overtime hours rates, holiday and weekend rates), Meridian's Mark-on-
Cost Pricing Methodology, and a table of show up fees (SUF) per location.

95. At the conclusion of her employment, Mbeki did not return to Meridian the Sony
USB Device from which she accessed the H-E-B Master Services Agreement on July 29, 2024.
As part of its investigation, Meridian searched its offices and files for the Sony USB Device
and has not located it.

96. Mbeki misappropriated the H-E-B Master Services Agreement, which contains
Meridian's trade secrets.

97. Access to Meridian's highly confidential documents, including but not limited
to the DRIFTWOOD ENTERPRISES, INC. Master Services Agreement, would be a windfall to a competitor, such as Alliance
Services, providing it with an enormous and unfair competitive advantage regarding, among other
things, allowing them to know of Meridian's financial data, existing rates, methodology for
calculation of mark-ups, and the overall strategy of the Company.

98. There was no Meridian business reason for Mbeki to remove Meridian's
highly confidential documents, including but not limited to the H-E-B Master Services
Agreement.

99. Further, on August 2, 2024 at 8:23 p.m., Mbeki also sent a Meridian document, an
Excel spreadsheet named "FM Store Assignment for all Regions 08 02 2024 Update.xlsx" ("H-
E-B Store Assignment"), to her personal e-mail at aelson0879@hotmail.com containing
information regarding DRIFTWOOD ENTERPRISES, INC.'s store locations, square footage of the premises occupied, customer
contact information, and other related information.

100. Mbeki had no business need to send this document to her personal e-mail account
while knowing that she was on the way out of the Company and were going to join a direct
competitor of Meridian, to which she was already secretly providing assistance. This conduct
was not in Meridian's interest and was against Meridian's interest.

101. Mbeki misappropriated the Company's trade secrets contained in the DRIFTWOOD ENTERPRISES, INC. Store
Assignment document.

102. Upon information and belief, Mbeki removed the H-E-B Master Services
Agreement and H-E-B Store Assignment to use and disclose them at her new employment at
Larkspur Capital, Inc. and to the benefit of Larkspur Capital, Inc.

103. The full extent of Meridian's trade secrets misappropriated by Mbeki and
Larkspur Capital, Inc. is not yet fully known as Meridian's investigation continues.

FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION
(Breach of the Hargrove Agreement)
(against Hargrove)

104. Meridian incorporates by reference its allegations above as if fully re-written.

105. A valid agreement exists between Meridian and Hargrove containing certain post-
employment restrictions that Hargrove promised to comply with in exchange for consideration.

106. Under the Hargrove Agreement, Hargrove agreed that for two years after termination of
his employment with Meridian, he will not "engage, participate, assist, hold any interest in,
or invest in any Competing Business, as defined in the Hargrove Agreement, which is located or
